summary.objective: Decide whether to retain and investigate the current J12 connector or evaluate a replacement, without changing the board pinout.
summary.headline: Evidence is insufficient for a J12 connector change: one synthetic note (naming Rover Beta, not Rover Alpha) reports two vibration-run disconnects with no measurement, profile, retention value, pin mapping or board revision.

sourceRegister.name: Field observation note — Rover Beta J12 (synthetic)

anchors.excerpt: SYNTHETIC FIXTURE. This note is invented for demonstration. It is not a real field report.
Rover Beta, Robotics & Industrial demonstration unit.
An operator reported two intermittent J12 connector disconnects during a vibration run.
The drive controller lost its sensor-harness link briefly and recovered.
No measurement, vibration profile, retention value, pin mapping or board revision is recorded in this note.
No other document accompanies this note.

knownFacts.statement: The source is a synthetic fixture invented for demonstration and is not a real field report.
An operator reported two intermittent J12 connector disconnects during a vibration run.
The drive controller lost its sensor-harness link briefly and recovered.
The note records no measurement, vibration profile, retention value, pin mapping or board revision.
No other document accompanies the note.
The note describes the unit as 'Rover Beta, Robotics & Industrial demonstration unit', whereas the frozen request names 'Rover Alpha (synthetic demonstration unit)'.

alternatives.title: Retain and investigate the current J12 connector
alternatives.description: Keep the existing J12 connector and pinout and investigate the root cause of the reported intermittent disconnects (e.g. mating/retention, harness strain relief, contact condition). Inference: the note does not establish whether the connector itself, the harness, or another element caused the link loss.
prerequisites: Identify the current J12 connector part and board revision
Obtain the vibration profile of the run in which disconnects occurred
Inspect the affected J12 mating pair and sensor harness
Confirm which unit (Rover Alpha vs Rover Beta) the observation applies to

alternatives.title: Evaluate a replacement J12 connector (pinout unchanged)
alternatives.description: Evaluate a candidate replacement connector that preserves the board pinout. No candidate is named and compatibility (footprint, pin mapping, retention, vibration performance) is unknown until evidenced.
prerequisites: Documented current J12 pin mapping and footprint
Root-cause evidence that the connector, not the harness or another element, is responsible

affectedArtifacts.basis: Inference: the disconnects occurred during a vibration run, but no vibration profile is recorded.

evidenceGaps.gap: No vibration profile or measurement recorded for the run in which disconnects occurred.
evidenceGaps.whyItMatters: Without the excitation conditions and measurements, the failure cannot be reproduced or compared against connector capability.

evidenceGaps.gap: No retention value or current J12 connector identification is recorded.
evidenceGaps.whyItMatters: Retention and part identity are needed to judge whether the existing connector is adequate or a replacement is warranted.

evidenceGaps.gap: No pin mapping or board revision is recorded.
evidenceGaps.whyItMatters: The goal requires an unchanged pinout; any replacement cannot be assessed for compatibility without the current mapping and board revision.

evidenceGaps.gap: Unit identity conflict: the note names Rover Beta while the request names Rover Alpha.
evidenceGaps.whyItMatters: It is unknown whether the observation applies to the product under review; both statements are recorded and neither is assumed correct.

evidenceGaps.gap: Only a single operator report of two events exists; no corroborating document, inspection or root-cause analysis.
evidenceGaps.whyItMatters: A single anecdotal note cannot distinguish connector failure from harness, cabling or controller causes.

reviewQuestions.question: Does the field observation apply to Rover Alpha, or only to Rover Beta?
reviewQuestions.prerequisite: Unit and board revision records for the observed unit

reviewQuestions.question: What vibration profile was applied during the run, and can the disconnects be reproduced with logged measurements?
reviewQuestions.prerequisite: Vibration run record and test setup

reviewQuestions.question: What is the current J12 connector part, its retention specification, and the board pin mapping?
Does inspection of the J12 mating pair and sensor harness indicate the connector, the harness, or another element as the cause?
reviewQuestions.prerequisite: Access to the affected unit and harness

nextAction.action: Collect the vibration-run record and current J12 identification (part, retention spec, pin mapping, board revision) for the observed unit, and confirm whether it is Rover Alpha or Rover Beta, before any connector change is considered.
nextAction.ownerRole: Hardware engineering lead with test engineering
nextAction.requiredInput: Vibration profile/measurements of the run, BOM/schematic for J12, board revision, unit identity

limitations: Packet ready means the paid preparation artifact was delivered. It is not engineering approval, a completed test or permission to release hardware. Independent engineering review and relevant physical evidence remain required.
